discovery: Discovery of transiting exoplanets and the photometric transit method that revealed the prevalence of small planets in the Galaxy
motivation: In 1999 Charbonneau and Henry independently observed the first exoplanet transit, HD 209458b. It confirmed that radial-velocity planets are real gas giants and gave their radii, densities and, later, the first atmospheric detections. Borucki spent decades arguing, against widespread scepticism, that space photometry at the parts-per-hundred-thousand level was achievable. He led the Kepler mission, which found thousands of planets and showed that small, rocky-sized planets, including temperate ones, are common around Sun-like stars. Transits turned exoplanets from points on a velocity curve into physical worlds that can be measured. They are the basis of today's characterisation of planetary atmospheres and of the search for habitable environments. This was a precision measurement that opened a new field and changed how we understand our place in the cosmos.
